hints.title: Triplet Search Complexity Obstacle
hints.text: Checking all triplets (i, j, k) directly requires O(N^3) time. How can traversing backward and maintaining the largest possible middle-value candidate detect if a smaller prefix element completes the required trio?

hints.title: Reverse Monotonic Decreasing Candidate Invariant
hints.text: When traversing backward, keep a monotonic decreasing list of candidates for '3'. Whenever an incoming element is larger than candidates, pop them to maximize s3 (candidate for '2'). Any earlier element < s3 completes the 132 pattern.

hints.title: Backward Candidate Tracking Procedure
hints.text: Initialize s3 to negative infinity and an empty candidate list. Traverse nums from right to left: if nums[i] < s3, return true. While the candidate list is non-empty and nums[i] > list[-1], set s3 = list.pop(). Append nums[i] to the candidate list. If the loop finishes, return false.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of array nums (1 <= N <= 2 * 10^5)
complexity.notes: Each element is pushed and popped at most once during reverse traversal.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute-force testing all triplets takes O(N^3) time; fixing i and j still takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining candidates for the '3' element in an auxiliary list enables finding the '1' element in strictly O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing the advantage of reverse traversal and understanding how s3 represents the best candidate for '2'.
